title: Weak-equivalence invariance of path-model homotopy pullbacks
statement: Use the simplicial sets, quasicategories, spaces and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in its fixed universe convention. Let $u:U\to W$, $v:V\to W$, $u':U'\to W'$, and $v':V'\to W'$ be maps of Kan complexes. Suppose that $a:U\to U'$, $b:V\to V'$, and $c:W\to W'$ are weak homotopy equivalences satisfying $cu=u'a$ and $cv=v'b$. Write $P(u,v)=U\times_{W,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,W}V$, and define $P(u',v')$ by the same formula. Then the map $P(u,v)\to P(u',v')$ sending $(x,y,\gamma)$ to $(a(x),b(y),c\circ\gamma)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 3.4.0.9 (032B), with path model Construction 3.4.0.3 (010B). Read online 2026-10-16, not archived in literature/. Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: For $W$ Kan, transpose a horn lifting problem for $e_W=(\operatorname{ev}_0,\operatorname{ev}_1):\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)\to W\times W$ to the extension problem from $(\Delta^1\times\Lambda_k^n)\amalg_{\partial\Delta^1\times\Lambda_k^n}(\partial\Delta^1\times\Delta^n)$ to $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n$ with target $W$. The boundary inclusion is a monomorphism, and a horn inclusion is anodyne because every Kan fibration lifts against it by definition. The pushout-product lemma makes the displayed inclusion anodyne, so it lifts against $W\to\Delta^0$; hence $e_W$ is a Kan fibration. This applies with $W\prime$ in place of $W$ as well.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.3 (00TM), endpoint special case; product/exponential adjunction and the cited pushout-product statement give the lifting argument explicitly.

proof.text: Apply the Kan-target testing characterization of weak homotopy equivalences to $c:W\to W\prime$. Testing at $W$ gives a map $d:W\prime\to W$ with $[dc]=[1_W]$ in the edge-component set of $\operatorname{Fun}(W,W)$. Postcomposition with $c$ gives $[cdc]=[c]$; injectivity of the same testing map at target $W\prime$ then gives $[cd]=[1_{W\prime}]$. Each equality means a finite zigzag of simplicial homotopies, since edge components are vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by edges.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13 (00UB), surjectivity/injectivity construction of the inverse; only finite edge zigzags are needed here.

proof.text: For a small simplicial set $K$, let $q=c_*:\operatorname{Fun}(K,W)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,W\prime)$ and $r=d_*$ in the opposite direction. For $T\in\{W,W\prime\}$, an edge $H:T\times\Delta^1\to T$ between two endomorphisms gives an edge between their postcomposition maps by the formula $(\varphi,t)\mapsto[k\mapsto H(\varphi(k),t)]$, interpreted by the internal-functor adjunction; thus Step 2 gives finite homotopy zigzags $rq\simeq1$ and $qr\simeq1$. For every Kan target $Z$, writing $L$ for either induced homotopy on an internal functor object, precomposition gives an edge of maps into $Z$ by $(\psi,t)\mapsto\psi\circ L_t$, so $q^*$ and $r^*$ are inverse bijections on the edge-component sets of maps into $Z$. The testing characterization therefore makes $q$ a weak homotopy equivalence. Take $K=\Delta^1$ to obtain the path-object vertical weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.5.2 (0149), final postcomposition-with-homotopy-inverse argument, expanded using the Kan-target testing characterization; 0149 itself states a realization mapping-space comparison, not general postcomposition invariance.

proof.text: Realization preserves finite products by the cited finite-limit statement. For topological products, a path or a based cube map is precisely a pair of paths or cube maps, and a homotopy relative to the boundary is precisely a pair of such homotopies; consequently $\pi_0(A\times B)=\pi_0(A)\times\pi_0(B)$ and $\pi_n(A\times B,(x,y))=\pi_n(A,x)\times\pi_n(B,y)$. Thus $a\times b$ and $c\times c$ are weak homotopy equivalences, including empty factors. Consider the cospans $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)\xrightarrow{e_W}W\times W\xleftarrow{(u,v)}U\times V$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W\prime)\xrightarrow{e_{W\prime}}W\prime\times W\prime\xleftarrow{(u\prime,v\prime)}U\prime\times V\prime$. Their vertical maps are $c_*$, $c\times c$, and $a\times b$. The left square commutes because $\operatorname{ev}_i(c\gamma)=c\operatorname{ev}_i(\gamma)$ for $i=0,1$, and the right square commutes because $cu=u\prime a$ and $cv=v\prime b$.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.9 (032B), displayed endpoint cospans; finite-product weak equivalences expanded using realization finite limits and the cubical definition.

proof.text: Apply weak-equivalence invariance of strict pullbacks along Kan fibrations to the two cospans from Step 4: the two left legs are fibrations by Step 1, and all three vertical maps are weak homotopy equivalences by Steps 3 and 4. Degreewise the upper pullback consists of $(x,y,\gamma)$ with $\operatorname{ev}_0(\gamma)=u(x)$ and $\operatorname{ev}_1(\gamma)=v(y)$, hence is exactly $P(u,v)$; the lower pullback is $P(u\prime,v\prime)$. The induced map is $(x,y,\gamma)\mapsto(a(x),b(y),c\circ\gamma)$, as required.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.4.0.9 (032B), application of Proposition 3.4.0.2 (0109) and Construction 3.4.0.3 (010B).
